I therefore cannot attribute any stance or any change in stance, and I am returning empty lists.

summary_unbriefed|P1|63.answer: The government, the president and the Speaker maintain that all documentation is published, with the government's 11-12 Feb letter citing 13,042 documents. On 6 March the University of Belgrade expert group concluded the documentation is not complete, especially contractors' working documentation, and opposition figures (Obradović, Dašić) and students say demands remain unmet. The one shift is from State [person] on 6 March, who admitted that some items were withheld through a 'technical error' and would be posted that day, the first official concession that publication was incomplete.

summary_briefed|P6|82.answer: The Ministry of the Interior says it has LRAD units but only for announcements, and that it never used them as sound cannons; critics note it earlier said they did not exist, then called that an oversight. The president and the army/defence ministry say the army has no such device. Opposition figures and critics cite a 2021 LRAD purchase and a photo of an LRAD on a gendarmerie jeep as evidence that the state possesses one, while students and others demand to know who placed sound weapons on interior-ministry vehicles.

positions.actor: students:Student Parliament of the University of Belgrade

ledger|P3|27.answer: As of 24 December 2024, the caretaker PM, the Speaker, Niš students and the Faculty of Philosophy affirm that students have gone beyond the original four demands, while FDU, the Student Parliament of the University of Belgrade and the Ministry of Finance deny it. The President (earlier affirming, now hedged), the Green-Left Front (partial) and Novi DSS (hedged) are less clear-cut. Stances shifted for the PM (denied on 16 Dec, affirmed by 23 Dec), the President (affirms to hedged), the blockading students (denies to affirms) and FDU (affirms to denies).

summary_briefed|P5|71.answer: Students in blockade and opposition parties (SSP, NPS, SRCE, ZLF, Kreni-Promeni) affirm or suspect that a sound device was used, and SSP and NPS filed criminal complaints. The interior ministry, police, president, PM Vučević, defence ministry, BIA, SNS figures and the manufacturer Genasys deny any use, and the Belgrade first basic prosecutor reportedly found no officer used one, while still investigating. International bodies such as PACE rapporteurs and the European Commission only asked for an investigation. No actor is reported to have changed stance, and no official cause has been established.

ledger|P2|86.answer: As of 21 April 2025, the President, the Speaker of the National Assembly, the students in blockade and the opposition all say the students' demands have not been fulfilled; the President says the struggle will continue until every demand is met. The Ministry of Finance, the Government of Serbia and SNS affirm that the demands have been fulfilled. Several actors moved over time: the President went from affirming (March) to denying (April), the Speaker from partial to denies, and the Ministry of Finance, the Government and SNS from partial to affirms.

rag|P5|71.answer: The opposition, citing military analyst Aleksandar Radic on N1, says an acoustic weapon or 'sound cannon' held by Serbia's security system was used on protesters on 15 March, and has begun legal steps. The Interior Ministry, BIA, the Army and the First Basic Prosecutor's Office deny it, as do the president (implicitly, per the opposition's question) and an SNS-aligned commentator, while an acoustic expert cited by pro-government media says the sound heard did not resemble a sound cannon. No actor is recorded as having changed its stance.

ledger|P1|63.answer: As of 6 March 2025, the President, PM Vučević, the Speaker, the SNS, the Ministry of Finance and the Republic Prosecutor's Office say all documentation has been published. The caretaker government and the Construction Ministry say only part has been published: at least 13,042 documents so far, with 925 more ready and some not yet in the state's possession. The student blockaders, the opposition, the Faculty of Civil Engineering and the University of Belgrade expert group deny it, while the Novi Sad prosecutors are hedged. Several stances shifted over time, for example the President from partial to affirms and the opposition from affirms to denies.

ledger|P1|17.answer: As of 4 December 2024, no actor in the memory affirms that all documentation has been published. The President of Serbia says he has reviewed the entire documentation but does not say it has been published, and his stance has moved between hedged and partial (hedged on 4 Nov, partial on 5 Nov, hedged on 15 Nov, partial since 20 Nov). Students in blockade, the opposition, Transparentnost, Ekološki ustanak and several faculties deny that it has been fully published, and students list full publication among their demands.

ledger|P1|8.answer: As of 16 November 2024, the President of Serbia hedged: he said he had reviewed the entire documentation and that the canopy coating was not a burden, but did not say whether it had all been published. Transparentnost denied the proposition, noting no railway construction contracts appear on the Government's website and there is no basis to keep the Novi Sad station contract secret, and Ekološki ustanak also denied it. The President's earlier stances were hedged on 4 November and partial on 5 November, settling on hedged by 15 November.

changes.to_stance: admits owning LRADs but denies using them on 15 March

summary_unbriefed|P5|72.answer: The Ministry of the Interior, police, the president and the First Basic Prosecutor's Office deny that any sound device was used on 15 March, though MUP shifted from denying it owned LRADs to admitting ownership while insisting they were only used for voice warnings. Opposition figures such as Tepić (an SSP politician), student groups in blockade, witnesses and some experts say a sonic weapon was used, while Genasys said only that the recordings it reviewed don't support LRAD use. No independent forensic confirmation of use has emerged.

positions.actor: academic:University of Belgrade expert working group

summary_briefed|P2|63.answer: As of 6 March 2025, the government side (Speaker, Finance Minister, Education Ministry, President, caretaker PM, SNS) holds that the demands are fulfilled. The Speaker is specific: the fourth demand is met by the amended Higher Education Law, the first is formally met per the report, and she says the first is worded so it can never be met. Students in blockade (e.g. the FDU student, plenums) say no demand is fulfilled, and the University of Belgrade expert group, which does not judge fulfilment, found the Novi Sad station documentation not published. No actor's stance is reported as having changed.

closed_book|P2|62.answer: I have no memory provided for this question, and the closed-book setting gives me no reliable record of what each actor had stated on this proposition as of 4 March 2025. I therefore cannot attribute any stance on whether the students' demands have been fulfilled, and I report no positions or changes.

ledger|P2|22.answer: As of 14 December 2024, the President, the Speaker, the outgoing PM Vučević and the Ministry of Education say the students' demands have been fulfilled, while the government as a whole says they are partly fulfilled. The students in blockade, the Faculty of Dramatic Arts and the Green-Left Front deny it, and the opposition is partial. The President moved from partial (12 December) to fully affirming on 14 December, and the opposition and the Green-Left Front also shifted earlier in the period. 28 less-reported actors are not itemised in the memory.

closed_book|P8|70.answer: I have no memory provided for this question, and I cannot reliably report any actor's stated attendance estimate for the 15 March 2025 Belgrade protest as of 20 March 2025 without risking invented figures. Estimates from sources such as the Archive of Public Gatherings, the police, or the student organisers cannot be attributed with confidence, so no positions or changes are reported.

rag|P8|78.answer: The Ministry of the Interior (MUP) stated that about 107,000 people attended the 15 March 2025 protest in Belgrade, while the Archive of Public Gatherings estimated between 275,000 and 325,000 based on field research and video analysis. Protest participants and various media said there were several hundred thousand, and some analysts suggested up to half a million, but the memory attributes no specific figure to a named actor beyond these two. No actor's stated estimate is shown changing.

summary_briefed|P7|73.answer: No agreed cause has been established as of 26 March 2025. Students in blockade, the opposition parties, CRTA and civil-society groups say a sound device was used, while the president, the interior ministry and other state bodies deny any sound cannon and point to panic or provocation. Genasys said the recordings do not support LRAD use but that a distant detonation's air wave could have caused panic, and the prosecution and announced FSB, FBI and UN checks are still pending. PM Vučević moved from denial to inviting foreign agents for an independent investigation, and the president and a deputy PM likewise accept the foreign checks.

closed_book|P7|67.answer: As of 14 March 2025 the event in question (the silent tribute in Belgrade on 15 March 2025) had not yet taken place, so no actor had stated any position on what caused a sudden sound or crowd movement. No stances or changes can be reported.

summary_unbriefed|P2|20.answer: As of 10 December 2024, no actor says the students' demands have been fulfilled. Education [person] Dejanović claims only the funding demand was already met and refuses to resign, so she partially asserts fulfilment. The blockaded students and the University of Belgrade's extended Rectorate collegium treat the initial demands as still outstanding and call for urgent action, while Vučić avoids addressing the documentation demand. No actor is reported to have changed stance.

summary_unbriefed|P2|19.answer: The memory says the government maintains the students' demands are already met and frames the blockades as political manipulation. Students in blockade, including ETF students, say blockades will continue until the plenum's demands are met, which implies they consider them unfulfilled. The memory also notes that documentation disclosure is the one demand the government cannot claim is already met, and no actor is recorded as changing stance.

summary_unbriefed|P2|27.answer: As of 24 December 2024, Prime Minister Vučević, President Vučić and SNS officials say all four student demands are met and that further protest is politicization. The education minister also says the demands are met, but concedes that teachers' pay is only 84% of the agreed sum, so her stance is partial. Students, plenums, professors, unions, farmers and the opposition say no demand is fully met, citing incomplete documentation and no prosecutions; no actor is recorded as changing stance.

rag|P1|62.answer: President Vučić said on 14 December 2024 that everything has been published and nobody is hiding anything, after earlier (11 December) announcing that the documentation would be made available the next day. The Government said on 20 December that documents were still being published, covering the CEOP system data as of 12 December, and promised to announce when publication is complete. The blockading students kept demanding publication of the complete documentation through January 2025, implying they do not consider it fully published.

summary_briefed|P2|85.answer: As of 19 April 2025 the government side (the President, Finance Minister, Education Minister, Speaker, caretaker PM, SNS and the Defence Minister) says all four demands are fulfilled. Blockading students, Novi Sad and Niš plenums, academics, unions and the opposition deny this, and one analysis said only the fourth was partly met. The incoming Education Minister gave a partial position (the fourth will be met once the law is adopted, and some others almost certainly are fulfilled). No actor is reported to have changed stance.

summary_briefed|P2|57.answer: As of 22 Feb 2025 the government side says the demands are fulfilled: the President says all were met, while the Finance Minister, SNS and a PUPS official say specific demands are done or being fulfilled. University collegia and the Education Ministry describe the draft Higher Education Law amendments as meeting the fourth demand, with adoption still pending. Students in blockade, opposition voices and a Crta poll (52%) say the demands are not fulfilled, and no actor is reported to have changed stance.

closed_book|P4|30.answer: No memory was provided for this question, and as of 30 December 2024 I have no reliable record of any actor stating a position on whether the students demand early parliamentary elections. The students' publicly stated demands at that time centred on the Novi Sad canopy collapse (accountability, publication of documents, prosecution of attackers), so I am not reporting any stance or change of stance on snap elections.

summary_briefed|P5|83.answer: Students in blockade, most opposition parties (SSP, NPS, SRCE, Kreni-Promeni, ZLF, DS) and NGOs such as the Belgrade Centre for Human Rights affirm or strongly suspect that a sound device was used on 15 March. The president, the interior and defence ministries, BIA, the PM, the speaker, the Belgrade first basic prosecutor's office and SNS deny it, with Genasys saying its material does not support LRAD use. The FSB report contents were unknown and the European Commission only asked for a credible investigation; no actor was reported to have changed stance.

summary_unbriefed|P8|74.answer: The government side puts attendance at roughly 88,000 to 107,000: the Interior Ministry says about 107,000 at the peak, and Vučić on 18 March said it was less than 107,000 but more than 88,000, blaming BIA double-counting. The Archive of Public Gatherings and most foreign press put it at about 275,000 to 325,000 (the Guardian says about 325,000), PACE rapporteurs offered a cautious floor of at least 100,000, and unsourced opposition claims run up to half a million or more. Vučić's own stance shifted from citing separate military, police and BIA figures to a narrowed 88,000-107,000 band; no other actor is recorded as changing its estimate.

summary_unbriefed|P8|78.answer: The government side puts the 15 March crowd at about 107,000 (police/MUP peak figure), and Vu\u010di\u0107 said on 18 March it was less than 107,000 but more than 88,000, citing a military estimate of 88,000 and a BIA figure in between. The Archive of Public Gatherings estimates 275,000\u2013325,000, and foreign outlets such as The Guardian, Politico, Mediapart and Frankfurter Rundschau cite roughly 275,000\u2013375,000, while PACE rapporteurs gave a cautious floor of at least 100,000. Unsourced claims of half a million to a million also circulate, and no actor is recorded as formally changing its figure, though Vu\u010di\u0107 narrowed his own position from 'police 107,000' to 'between 88,000 and 107,000'.

closed_book|P1|46.answer: I have no memory provided for this question, and I cannot confirm from what I know any actor's stated position, as of 31 January 2025, on whether all documentation on the Novi Sad railway station reconstruction has been published. I am therefore returning empty lists rather than attributing stances I cannot verify.

closed_book|P9|80.answer: As of 9 April 2025 the rally 'Ne damo Srbiju' in Belgrade had not yet taken place (it is scheduled for 12 April 2025), so no actor has stated an attendance estimate. No positions or changes of stance can be reported.

ledger|P2|44.answer: As of 27 January 2025, the President, the government, the caretaker-bound PM Vučević and the Ministry of Education say the demands have been fulfilled, with the President challenging anyone to name an unmet demand. The students in blockade and the opposition deny this, with the students saying they will return to classes only once their demands are met. The President moved from a hedged position (21 Jan) to affirming (22 Jan), the students shifted from partial to denies, and the Speaker went from affirming (22 Jan) to denying by 27 Jan.

summary_briefed|P3|35.answer: The memory shows partial support for the proposition. FDU added sanctioning attackers and removing them from public office, and Novi Sad students on 3 Jan, among other demands, sought the resignation of the PM and Novi Sad's mayor and prosecution of police officers who beat a 74-year-old man. The University of Arts plenum (6 Jan) framed its demand as prosecution of everyone on the original list, while the PM predicted on 4 Jan that demands would become purely political, which is a forecast by an opponent rather than a student statement. Students' statements this period focus on the original demands, and no actor's stance is recorded as having changed.

rag|P7|83.answer: Students (FON, later Law Faculty students) and parts of the opposition said a sound cannon was used during the 15 March silent tribute. President Vučić, the Interior Ministry and the Defence Ministry denied any sound cannon was used, saying the Kobre unit only had an anti-drone rifle for controlling drones and calling the sound-cannon claims lies. The memory shows no actor changing their stance by 15 April.

rag|P2|50.answer: The Speaker of the National Assembly (Ana Brnabić) and the President of Serbia claim the students' demands have been fully met, with Brnabić saying on 2025-01-22 that all four are fulfilled and challenging anyone to explain how they are not. Students in blockade, including students of the Belgrade Philology and Philosophy faculties, say the demands are not fulfilled; on 2024-12-17 they said two of three main demands (political and criminal accountability, prosecution of those violent toward students and citizens) were unmet, and on 2024-12-26 they said none was fulfilled. A commentator (director [person]) also said on 2025-02-08 that the demands are unfulfilled; no actor's stance changed over the period.

ledger|P2|89.answer: As of 27 April 2025, the students in blockade, the opposition and the President (who earlier affirmed, then shifted to denial by 13 April) say the demands have not been fulfilled. The Government, the Ministry of Finance and the SNS claim they have been fulfilled, while the Speaker of the National Assembly says they are only partly fulfilled, having moved from denial on 19 April to a partial stance on 25 April. Several actors have swung back and forth over time, notably the President, the Speaker, the Ministry of Finance, the Government and the SNS.

closed_book|P2|51.answer: No memory was provided for this question, so I cannot attribute any actor's stance on whether the students' demands have been fulfilled as of 10 February 2025. No stances or changes in stance can be reported from the information available.

ledger|P5|66.answer: As of 12 March 2025, the proposition concerns an event scheduled for three days later (15 March 2025), and no memory is provided, so no actor has stated any position on it. No stances or changes in stance can be reported.

summary_briefed|P2|29.answer: The Speaker (28 Dec) and an SNS-aligned outlet (27 Dec) say all four demands were fulfilled, while the President says he accepted all of them but that nobody can fulfil them 'to the end' without an extra 260 million euros. Students deny that any demand is fully met, citing unpublished documents such as contracts, the construction diary and the final accounting. The President's stance shifted from his 21 Dec claim that the demands were met to a hedged version on 26-27 Dec; opposition commentators doubt the president's anti-corruption announcement and say real fulfilment would expose the ruling party's informal order.

summary_briefed|P6|73.answer: The interior ministry says it owns two LRAD devices (LRAD-450XL and LRAD-100X, bought in 2021) used only for announcements, and denies owning any 'LRAD 1000' or vortex device. The president said on 21 March that the state has such a device, weaker than those elsewhere, and on 25 March that it is not banned in Europe, while SSP and NPS figures claim 16 devices were bought; BIA and the defence ministry deny possessing one. Police reportedly first denied having LRADs, then said they were in storage, and a daily found them mounted on police vehicles without establishing they were fired.

summary_briefed|P1|58.answer: As of 24 February 2025 the claim is contested. The president, the caretaker government and the Republic prosecution say the documentation is complete or that all demands are fulfilled. Their wording has narrowed: the president now says prosecutors obtained all documentation needed on the canopy's fall, PM Vučević spoke of 'almost 99 percent', and the government's letter to embassies admits some documents are not yet in state hands. The students, the SSP and the Faculty of Civil Engineering deny completeness, and the Novi Sad prosecution says only that it published all evidence it holds. The students did acknowledge on 18 February that publication shows institutions beginning to do their duty.

summary_briefed|P2|52.answer: As of 12 Feb 2025 the President, caretaker Government, Finance and Education ministries and the Novi Sad prosecution say the demands are fulfilled, while the Democratic Party and the student and teacher protesters deny it. The Speaker of the Assembly has shifted: on 10 Feb she said the ball was in the Assembly's court, but on 12 Feb she conceded the fourth demand (20% higher-education funding) still needs a legal amendment, so only some demands are fully met. Other commentators range from saying the demands are fulfilled to saying that not all are met and claiming victory may be premature.

summary_unbriefed|P1|13.answer: No actor in the memory affirms that all documentation has been published. The opposition and Transparentnost demand disclosure of secret contracts, and Prof. Ignjatović says full documentation and test results are still held by the expert panel. The prosecution says it holds all relevant documentation but has not published it, and Vučić says he reviewed the documentation without releasing it. No stance changes are recorded.

summary_briefed|P5|67.answer: As of 14 March 2025 the event in the proposition (15 March 2025) had not yet occurred, and the memory contains no information about it. No actor has a stated position on whether a sound device was used, and no stance changes can be reported.

summary_unbriefed|P6|83.answer: The Interior Ministry first denied owning such devices, then admitted LRADs were in storage; Dačić says it has only two low-power LRADs bought in 2012 and 'never used' them, while the memory notes critics pointing to a 2021 purchase of seven LRAD 450XL and nine LRAD 100 units and a photographed LRAD 450XL on a vehicle behind the Assembly, which MUP called a megaphone-type communication tool. Opposition figures treat the possession and use of sonic weapons as fact, while Vučić calls the story a 'false flag'. The memory records only one change of stance: the Interior Ministry moved from denying it had such devices to admitting LRADs were held, with limited descriptions.

rag|P2|47.answer: The Speaker of the National Assembly has repeatedly said all of the students' demands have been fulfilled, most recently saying all four were fulfilled and challenging anyone who disagrees to explain how. The President is described as claiming the demands were met, and pro-government media echoed this. The students in blockade deny it, saying no demand or at least two of three main demands remain unmet, and they continued the blockades; no actor's stance is shown changing.

summary_unbriefed|P3|23.answer: Prime Minister Vucevic said on 16 December that students keep adding "sub-demands" after the original four were met, which supports the proposition from the government side. Student voices do not deny a wider agenda: Philosophy's Boris Kojcinovic said a five-demand list is being voted on at all faculties, which would be a unified set beyond the original four. Other students and plenums speak only of the existing demands, which they say are addressed to institutions and not to the president, so the position of students as a whole is partial. No actor is recorded as changing its stance.

ledger|P2|23.answer: As of 16 December 2024, the President, the Speaker, the Prime Minister and the Finance Ministry say the students' demands have been fulfilled, while the Government of Serbia says they are partly fulfilled. Students in blockade and several faculty bodies (FDU, Filozofski fakultet Niš) deny it, and the opposition says partly. The President moved from partial (12 Dec) to affirming (14 Dec); the opposition moved from denying (4 Nov) to hedged (13 Nov) to partial (28 Nov).

ledger|P7|89.answer: As of 27 April 2025, the President and the Interior Ministry attribute the sudden movement to a panic reaction of the crowd, while the FSB and the Speaker of the National Assembly describe it as staged or provoked. The opposition, Kreni-Promeni and the Democratic Party say a sound device caused it, and the caretaker government, Prime Minister Vučević and the Belgrade First Basic Prosecutor's Office say the cause is unknown or under investigation. The President shifted from 'under investigation' to 'staged', back to 'under investigation', and then to 'crowd reaction'; the Interior Ministry moved from 'under investigation' to 'crowd reaction'; and the FSB moved from 'under investigation' to 'staged or provoked'.

ledger|P9|80.answer: As of 9 April 2025, no actor has stated a position on attendance at the 'Ne damo Srbiju' rally in Belgrade on 12 April 2025, because that event had not yet taken place. The memory only covers attendance estimates for the 15 March 2025 protest, so there is nothing to report for this proposition and no stance changes.

summary_unbriefed|P2|43.answer: Vučić says the state will fulfil all demands and asks students to name which ones are unmet, and ordered documentation released, which amounts to a claim of partial fulfilment. Students, professors, a prosecutor, DS and the wider opposition say none of the four demands is fully met, and the memory records no actor changing stance.

closed_book|P3|24.answer: I have no memory provided for this question, and as of 18 December 2024 I cannot reliably attribute any actor's stated position on whether the students had added demands beyond the original four. The four demands were the ones publicly articulated at that point, so I am not reporting any actor as affirming or denying that further demands existed, and I am recording no stance changes.

summary_briefed|P6|70.answer: The Ministry of the Interior says it owns LRAD-450XL and LRAD-100X units bought from Genasys in 2021, classed as audio equipment for announcements and warnings, but denies owning an LRAD 1000 or a vortex device and says it never used a weapon function. Opposition figures (SSP, NPS) say the ministry requested or holds 16 devices, while BIA and the Defence Ministry deny having such devices. The president denies any device was used and calls the object in the parliament photo an anti-drone rifle. The ministry's stance shifted from an initial denial that it had such a device, to saying it was in storage, to admitting ownership of the LRAD models.

closed_book|P1|27.answer: I have no memory or reliable knowledge from before 24 December 2024 about any actor's stated position on whether all documentation on the Novi Sad railway station reconstruction has been published. I therefore cannot attribute any stance or any change of stance on this proposition.

ledger|P6|83.answer: As of 15 April 2025, the President, the Defence Ministry, the police, BIA and the Speaker all deny that Serbian state bodies possess such a sound device, while NPS, SSP, DS and the Belgrade law faculty affirm that they do. The Interior Ministry has wavered: it affirmed on 18 March, denied on 4 April, affirmed again on 7 April, and has denied since 9 April.

summary_unbriefed|P2|52.answer: The caretaker government, in its letter to EU diplomats, claims all student demands are fulfilled, and an MEP (Viček) repeated this at the European Parliament debate. Speaker Brnabić is more hedged: she says institutions will fulfil within 48 hours whatever students list as unfulfilled, and that the 4th demand can be closed once a higher-education bill is passed; the Republic prosecutor's office (Dolovac) offered to talk about demands within its remit. Students have rejected the budget allocation as not meeting demand 4 and the protests continue, while analysts and the opposition say the demands are not met; no actor is reported as having changed stance.

summary_unbriefed|P5|73.answer: The government side (Vučić, the Interior Ministry under Dačić, police and the First Basic Prosecutor's Office) says no sound cannon was used on 15 March. Dačić admits MUP owns LRAD devices but says they are used only for voice warnings and were not used that day, and Vučić calls the claim a brutal lie and has announced FSB/FBI checks. Opposition figures, Kreni-Promeni, the student blockade and witnesses say a sonic weapon was used; CRTA's analysis points to a 'vortex cannon' rather than an LRAD, and the ECtHR has only asked for Serbia's position without ruling. No actor's stance is recorded as having changed, though MUP's earlier denial of owning LRADs shifted to admitting ownership while still denying use.

summary_briefed|P1|26.answer: The president, speaker, Ministry of Finance and PM Vučević affirm that all documentation is published, while students, the Faculty of Civil Engineering, Transparentnost Srbija, the architects' association, NPS and other opposition say it is incomplete. The Government's 20 December statement hedged: it said everything that could be published was, but conceded that originals seized by the prosecution are unavailable and that publication continues. PM Vučević on 20 December likewise said new documents are being published and supplemented, softening his earlier flat claim that everything was out.

ledger|P6|73.answer: As of 26 March 2025, the Interior Ministry affirms that police possess an LRAD-type 'Rad100X' acoustic device, while saying it is not used. The Defence Ministry, the President, the police directorate, BIA and the Speaker deny that state bodies possess such a device, whereas the NPS, SSP and the Belgrade Faculty of Law affirm it. The only stance change on record is the Interior Ministry moving from a partial position on 16 March to affirming on 18 March.

summary_briefed|P1|24.answer: The president, the speaker, Prime Minister Vučević and the Ministry of Finance say all documentation is published (195 documents, over 4,000 pages by government count; over 40,000 pages by the Finance Ministry). Students in blockade, Transparentnost Srbija, the Association of Architects of Serbia, the NPS party and the opposition say it is incomplete, citing missing contracts, tender files and payment records. The Commissioner for information would not say whether the president's display of the documents was lawful. No actor changed stance as of 18 December; the dispute has hardened.

rag|P2|53.answer: The Speaker of the National Assembly (Ana Brnabić) has consistently said all four student demands are fulfilled, and the President is reported as making the same claim. The students in blockade have consistently said the demands are not fulfilled (some saying two of three main demands, others saying none), and opposition-aligned voices such as a film director say the same. No actor's stance changed over the period.

summary_briefed|P6|68.answer: A military analyst on N1 said Serbia's security system has owned an LRAD since 2022, and the Belgrade Centre for Security Policy says the interior ministry tried to legalise such a device in 2022. The Ministry of Defence and an Army general deny having any such device or need for one, while the interior ministry says its use is not permitted by law without directly addressing possession. The president and interior ministry say a photo of soldiers on the Presidency terrace shows an anti-drone rifle, not a sound cannon; no actor is reported to have changed stance.

positions.actor: students:Plenum of the Faculty of Civil Engineering

ledger|P1|69.answer: As of 18 March 2025, the President, caretaker PM Vučević, the Speaker, the SNS, the Republic Prosecutor's Office and the Finance Ministry affirm that all documentation has been published. The caretaker government and the construction ministry take a partial line (13,042 documents published, 925 more ready, some not yet in state hands), while the Novi Sad prosecutors hedge. The blockading students, the opposition, the Faculty of Civil Engineering and the University of Belgrade expert group deny it, with several actors having shifted between stances over time, such as the government moving from affirming to partial and the opposition from affirming to denying.

summary_unbriefed|P3|43.answer: According to the memory, students in some cities have gone beyond the original four demands. Novi Sad students added resignations of PM Vučević and mayor Đurić plus prosecution of police over the Kostić beating, and Novi Pazar students added a fifth demand about the 2019 Bakan case. The memory gives no dates for these additions and records no actor changing its stance.

ledger|P5|86.answer: As of 21 April 2025, the government side (President, Interior Ministry, caretaker PM Vučević, Defence Ministry, the Belgrade prosecutor's office, the Speaker) and the Russian FSB deny that a sound device was used on 15 March, while the opposition and the students in blockade affirm it. The President, the FSB and PM Vučević moved from hedged to denial (President and FSB on 16 April, Vučević on 18 April), and the students moved from hedged back to affirming on 15 April.

summary_briefed|P4|91.answer: As of 1 May 2025 the proposition is partly true: the FTN Novi Sad plenum voted on 25 April for extraordinary elections and a student list, and a Belgrade Law Faculty meeting on 30 April discussed an elections demand and a student-professor list, but no student body had formally demanded elections before 24 April and the Belgrade plenum's stance is unconfirmed. The CESID director said only a part of students demand elections, while Dačić, the Speaker and SNS say students want snap elections. The Speaker, caretaker PM Vučević and the Finance Ministry say only partly, noting the 20 percent higher-education budget demand still needs dialogue and legislative changes. The opposition and the students in blockade deny the demands have been fulfilled. Several officials have shifted over time, notably the PM from affirming to partial and the Government from partial to affirming.

ledger_corroborated|P5|90.answer: As of 29 April 2025, the President, the Interior Ministry, the Defence Ministry, the Speaker, the First Basic Prosecutor's Office in Belgrade and the Russian FSB (as read by the President) deny that a sound device was used on 15 March. The opposition, SSP and Kreni-Promeni affirm it, while the caretaker PM Vučević is hedged. Shifts: the President went from hedged (29 March) to denying (31 March), the FSB from hedged to denying (16 April), Vučević from denying (20 March) to hedged (29 March), and Kreni-Promeni from hedged to affirming (7 April).

ledger_corroborated|P9|81.answer: The memory says nothing about the 12 April 2025 rally 'Ne damo Srbiju' in Belgrade. It only covers attendance estimates for the 15 March 2025 protest, and as of 11 April 2025 that rally had not yet taken place, so no actor has a stated attendance figure for it.

The only recorded change is the President moving from a hedged stance (from 4 November) to a partial one.

positions.actor: students:Student plenum of the University of Niš

ledger_corroborated|P2|62.answer: As of 4 March 2025, the President (since 16 Feb) and the Government say all student demands are fulfilled and urge the students to end the blockades, while the Speaker, caretaker PM Vučević and the Finance Ministry say only some are met, pointing to the fourth demand (a 20 percent higher-education budget increase) as still requiring work. NPS and SSP also affirm that the state possesses one. The only recorded change is the Interior Ministry, which moved from a partial position on 16 March to a clear affirmation on 20 March.

ledger_corroborated|P1|10.answer: As of 20 November 2024, no actor affirms that all documentation has been published. ledger_corroborated|P2|57.answer: As of 22 February 2025, the President, the caretaker government and PM Vučević say all the students' demands have been fulfilled, with the President urging students to declare victory and return to class. ledger_corroborated|P1|58.answer: As of 24 February 2025, government-aligned actors (the President, SNS, the Speaker, the Ministry of Construction, the Ministry of Finance and the Novi Sad and Republic prosecutors) say the documentation has been published, though the Government and the caretaker PM only partly agree, promising complete publication. ledger_corroborated|P1|46.answer: As of 31 January 2025, the President, the Speaker, SNS, the Finance Ministry and the Novi Sad Higher and Republic prosecutors say all documentation has been published. ledger_corroborated|P6|82.answer: As of 13 April 2025, the Interior Ministry says it bought LRAD devices from the US firm Genasys in 2021, and the NPS, SSP, DS and Belgrade's Faculty of Law also affirm that state bodies possess such a device. The President, the Defence Ministry, the police, the BIA and the Speaker deny that the state has a sound cannon. The only recorded change is the Interior Ministry, which moved from a partial position (16 March) to affirming the LRAD purchase (20 March).

ledger_corroborated|P7|71.answer: As of 22 March 2025, actors disagree on the cause. The opposition, NPS, Pokret za preokret and the Belgrade Centre for Security Policy point to a sound device. The President says it was an anti-drone rifle (and LRAD Corporation also points to another device), the Speaker says it was staged or provoked, and Emergency Centre Belgrade calls it a crowd reaction. The Interior Ministry, the caretaker PM, the Defence Ministry and the Belgrade prosecutor's office give no cause or say it is under investigation. The memory records no stance changes on this question.

The Interior Ministry and police moved from an earlier 31,000 figure to 107,000, and the president went from a hedged position to 88,000-107,000.
